lines.raw: The idea in one sentence.

lines.raw: **Utilization** metrics count **how much care** members use, and every cost PMPM is simply **how much care** × **price per unit**, so you can always tell whether costs rose because of more care or pricier care.
lines.say: Utilization metrics count how much care members use, and every cost P M P M is simply how much care × price per unit, so you can always tell whether costs rose because of more care or pricier care.

scenes.section: The US version: the core utilization metrics

lines.raw: Lone Star Health, utilization in 2025 (120,000 member months, illustrative).
lines.say: Lone Star Health, utilization in 2025 (120,000 member months, illustrative).

lines.raw: **Admissions per 1,000**. Formula: Admissions ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 720 admissions. Result: **72**.
lines.say: Admissions per 1,000. Formula: Admissions ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 720 admissions. Result: 72.

lines.raw: **Days per 1,000**. Formula: Hospital days ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 2,880 days. Result: **288**.
lines.say: Days per 1,000. Formula: Hospital days ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 2,880 days. Result: 288.

lines.raw: **ALOS** (average length of stay). Formula: Hospital days ÷ admissions. Count: 2,880 ÷ 720. Result: **4.0 days**.
lines.say: A L O S (average length of stay). Formula: Hospital days ÷ admissions. Count: 2,880 ÷ 720. Result: 4.0 days.

lines.raw: **ER visits per 1,000**. Formula: Emergency room visits ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 1,800 visits. Result: **180**.
lines.say: E R visits per 1,000. Formula: Emergency room visits ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 1,800 visits. Result: 180.

lines.raw: **Office visits per 1,000**. Formula: Office visits ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 24,000 visits. Result: **2,400**.
lines.say: Office visits per 1,000. Formula: Office visits ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 24,000 visits. Result: 2,400.

lines.raw: **Scripts per 1,000**. Formula: Prescriptions filled ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 120,000 scripts. Result: **12,000** (12 per member per year).
lines.say: Scripts per 1,000. Formula: Prescriptions filled ÷ member months × 12,000. Count: 120,000 scripts. Result: 12,000 (12 per member per year).

lines.raw: The key formula: PMPM = use × price.
lines.say: The key formula: P M P M = use × price.

scenes.section: The key formula: PMPM = use × price

lines.raw: Splitting a PMPM.
lines.say: Splitting a P M P M.

lines.raw: PMPM equals Utilization per 1,000 times Cost per unit ÷ 12,000.
lines.say: P M P M equals Utilization per 1,000 times Cost per unit ÷ 12,000.

lines.raw: For example: Inpatient: 72 admits per 1,000 times $18,000 per admit ÷ 12,000 equals $108.00 PMPM.
lines.say: For example: Inpatient: 72 admits per 1,000 times 18000 dollars per admit ÷ 12,000 equals 108 dollars P M P M.

lines.raw: Inpatient. Utilization per 1,000: 72 admits. Cost per unit: $18,000. PMPM: 72 × $18,000 ÷ 12,000 = **$108.00**.
lines.say: Inpatient. Utilization per 1,000: 72 admits. Cost per unit: 18000 dollars. P M P M: 72 × 18000 dollars ÷ 12,000 = 108 dollars.

lines.raw: ER (facility). Utilization per 1,000: 180 visits. Cost per unit: $2,000. PMPM: 180 × $2,000 ÷ 12,000 = **$30.00**.
lines.say: E R (facility). Utilization per 1,000: 180 visits. Cost per unit: 2000 dollars. P M P M: 180 × 2000 dollars ÷ 12,000 = 30 dollars.

lines.raw: Pharmacy. Utilization per 1,000: 12,000 scripts. Cost per unit: $90. PMPM: 12,000 × $90 ÷ 12,000 = **$90.00**.
lines.say: Pharmacy. Utilization per 1,000: 12,000 scripts. Cost per unit: 90 dollars. P M P M: 12,000 × 90 dollars ÷ 12,000 = 90 dollars.

Inpatient P M P M. 2024: 72 × 16500 dollars ÷ 12,000 = 99 dollars. 2025: 108 dollars. Change: +9.1 percent.

lines.raw: **Utilization is up** → look at care management, prior authorization or ways to keep members out of hospital (for example better primary care).
lines.say: Utilization is up to look at care management, prior authorization or ways to keep members out of hospital (for example better primary care).

lines.raw: **Unit cost is up** → look at provider contracts, where members get care (a cheaper hospital or setting), or drug choices.
lines.say: Unit cost is up to look at provider contracts, where members get care (a cheaper hospital or setting), or drug choices.

lines.raw: Both often move together; the split tells you which lever matters more.
lines.say: Both often move together; the split tells you which lever matters more.

lines.raw: Why it matters for data.
lines.say: Why it matters for data.

lines.raw: Counting units is harder than summing dollars.
lines.say: Counting units is harder than summing dollars.

lines.raw: One hospital stay can arrive as **several claims** (interim bills, a transfer between hospitals, an adjustment), so analysts must **combine claims into one admission** before counting.
lines.say: One hospital stay can arrive as several claims (interim bills, a transfer between hospitals, an adjustment), so analysts must combine claims into one admission before counting.

lines.raw: An ER visit that leads to admission is usually counted as part of the admission, not as an ER visit.
lines.say: An E R visit that leads to admission is usually counted as part of the admission, not as an E R visit.

lines.raw: Write the counting rules down, or admits per 1,000 will not match between reports.
lines.say: Write the counting rules down, or admits per 1,000 will not match between reports.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Utilization metrics count care per 1,000 members per year: admits, days, ER visits, office visits, scripts.
lines.say: Utilization metrics count care per 1,000 members per year: admits, days, E R visits, office visits, scripts.

lines.raw: ALOS = days ÷ admits.
lines.say: A L O S = days ÷ admits.

lines.raw: PMPM = utilization per 1,000 × cost per unit ÷ 12,000.
lines.say: P M P M = utilization per 1,000 × cost per unit ÷ 12,000.

lines.raw: If PMPM rises with flat utilization, the cause is unit cost (price or mix), and vice versa.
lines.say: If P M P M rises with flat utilization, the cause is unit cost (price or mix), and vice versa.

lines.raw: Units must be counted carefully: combine claims into stays, and decide how ER-to-admission is counted.
lines.say: Units must be counted carefully: combine claims into stays, and decide how E R to-admission is counted.
